verdicts.note: Tested toward -1: she started as an administrative assistant in 2015, was appointed in 2019 and was elected once, unopposed, in 2022 [S2][S3], so her elected tenure is short. Still, she is the sitting Assessor with 11 years in the office, seven of them heading it, and she asks for re-election explicitly on that record [S1][S2]. Against a challenger campaigning on change, that is the proven-record end of the axis. -2 high holds, though it is on the strong side.

He seeks his first elected office [S1] and frames the race as a change in how the office is run; on election night he said voters 'might want some change' [S3]. But he has more than 11 years as an appraiser and deputy assessor [S1], so this is a professional insider, not an outsider. +1 medium is right. No taxes score is right either: 'fair, transparent, and accurate valuations' is about valuation quality, not tax levels, and transparency talk is not reform evidence.
